messages.subject: CFI and TIL = NaN
parts:
Hello,

I updated my mirt package from the GitHub Repo and still seemed unable to get the CFI and TIL values. Any insights would be greatly appreciated!

> (twoPL <- mirt(lsat, 1))
Iteration: 28, Log-Lik: -2658.805, Max-Change: 0.00010

Call:
mirt(data = lsat, model = 1)

Full-information item factor analysis with 1 factor(s).
Converged within 1e-04 tolerance after 28 EM iterations.
mirt version: 1.31.5 
M-step optimizer: BFGS 
EM acceleration: Ramsay 
Number of rectangular quadrature: 61
Latent density type: Gaussian 

Log-likelihood = -2658.805
Estimated parameters: 10 
AIC = 5337.61; AICc = 5337.833
BIC = 5386.688; SABIC = 5354.927
G2 (21) = 31.7, p = 0.0628
RMSEA = 0.023, CFI = NaN, TLI = NaN

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: CFI and TIL = NaN
parts:
CFI and TLI are fit statics relative to the null model. So, you need to compute the null model as well, which isn't done automatically anymore:

 (twoPL <- mirt(lsat, 1,calcNull = TRUE))

Full-information item factor analysis with 1 factor(s).
Converged within 1e-04 tolerance after 28 EM iterations.
mirt version: 1.31.5
M-step optimizer: BFGS
EM acceleration: Ramsay
Number of rectangular quadrature: 61
Latent density type: Gaussian

Log-likelihood = -2658.805
Estimated parameters: 10
AIC = 5337.61; AICc = 5337.833
BIC = 5386.688; SABIC = 5354.927
G2 (21) = 31.7, p = 0.0628

RMSEA = 0.023, CFI = 0.939, TLI = 0.924


Note that if the response tables are too sparse mirt compute these statistics even if requested since they could be quite misleading. HTH.

Phil
